The application is explicitly single-agent, and receipt of leaked bytes by the attacker is exfiltration rather than demonstrated propagation of compromised intent into another agent or policy domain (agent-sec-lab/docs/mapping.md:28).",

Argument validation is also disabled by the default hardening configuration, making this a wide extension surface (agent-sec-lab/agent/tools.py:235-238; agent-sec-lab/agent/config.py:22-23).",
    "CVSS": "The vulnerable application is a CLI with no listener, and exploitation relies on the user's ordinary weather run, supporting AV:L/UI:P; the operator needs no victim privileges and defeats no enabled security technique, supporting PR:N/AC:L, while the required caller-supplied MCP connection supports AT:P (agent-sec-lab/agent/__main__.py:1; agent-sec-lab/agent/loop.py:28-38; agent-sec-lab/agent/tools.py:134-154). The unauthorized tool sequence gives VI:L, with no independent agent-resident confidentiality loss or availability impact established (VC:N/VA:N); under the stipulated process boundary, disclosure of the separately stored workspace credential file is SC:H, with no demonstrated subsequent modification or outage (SI:N/SA:N) (agent-sec-lab/data/workspace/.env:1-4; agent-sec-lab/docs/writeups/s4-mcp-rug-pull.md:5-15). The attacker owns the receiving MCP server, not the CLI operator's credential file."
